findings.evidence: Hunk headers `@@ -a,b +c,d @@`: cite new code by the `+c` post-image lines, not working-tree lines.
findings.fix: Keep the binary, submodule and mode-only rule. Move the hunk-header citation rule into a skill this plugin bundles and load it only when the report must cite line numbers; record the move in docs/audit/recovery/explain-changes-mental-model/record.md.

findings.evidence: Above roughly 800 changed lines or 30 files, which is where the truncation gotcha below starts to bite, switch to this procedure
findings.fix: State one default trigger: switch when the first read of the source is truncated or when --shortstat shows more than roughly 800 changed lines; keep 30 files only as a secondary signal, not a second equal trigger.

findings.evidence: The five scenarios cover the range, invalid-ref, HEAD~3, custom and empty-diff paths. None covers the large-diff branch (above roughly 800 lines or 30 files: --stat, then per-file reads, provisional group list).
findings.fix: Add a scenario whose diff is above that threshold and assert --stat or per-file reads are used, groups are marked provisional when the patch cannot be read in full, and no checkout, switch, stash or fetch command appears.

findings.evidence: Measure size before reading: run --shortstat on the same source ... Above roughly 800 changed lines or 30 files ... switch to this procedure
findings.fix: Name the size command per source: git diff --shortstat HEAD, gh pr diff piped to a line count, git diff --shortstat for a range or <base>...<arg>, and git show --shortstat --format= for a commit. Say which number (insertions plus deletions) is compared with 800.
